# forestsens-python -- LLM reference

Python client for the ForestSens forestry data-processing API. Upload drone imagery or LiDAR
point clouds, run a processing pipeline (orthomosaic, tree detection, segmentation, wheel-rut
assessment, ...), download the results.

Install: `pip install git+https://github.com/SmartForest-no/forestsens-python.git@v3.4.0`

Requires a ForestSens API key (`fs_...`) -- generated by the user in the ForestSens web app (Profile, then
API keys), or issued by an account admin on their behalf. Keys expire (365 days by default; an expired key
answers 401 "API key expired"). This client never creates one -- it only consumes an existing key. Never print
a key or write it into a file that is committed; if the key or the host is missing, ask the person.

## Setup

```python
from forestsens import Client

client = Client(gateway_host="...", api_key="fs_...")          # explicit
client = Client()                                               # or: FORESTSENS_GATEWAY_HOST / FORESTSENS_API_KEY env vars
client = Client(config_path="~/.forestsens/config.json")        # or: {"gateway_host": "...", "api_key": "..."} JSON file
```

## Client methods (full signatures)

```python
Client.list_pipelines(sens: str | None = None) -> list[Pipeline]
Client.find_pipeline(name: str, sens: str | None = None) -> Pipeline
    # Raises LookupError if no match, or more than one match.

Client.upload_files(
    paths: str | os.PathLike | list[str | os.PathLike],
    name: str | None = None,
    on_progress: Callable[[str, int, int], None] | None = None,
    project: str | dict | None = None,   # a Project, a project id or an exact project name
    private: bool = False,               # True: visible only to you, account admins and members you share it with
    concurrency: int = 4,                # files up to 16 MiB sent this many at a time; 1 = one after another
) -> str  # returns upload_id
    # paths: one file, one folder (its top-level files only, NOT recursive, dotfiles skipped),
    # or a list mixing either. Small files go up `concurrency` at a time; large files (>16 MiB) are then
    # chunked/resumed automatically, one after another.
    # on_progress(filename, loaded_bytes, total_bytes): 0 at the start of each file, about once per percent
    # while it uploads (per chunk for large files), total at the end. Silent when None.

Client.list_projects() -> list[Project]
Client.create_project(name) -> Project
Client.rename_project(project, name) -> Project
Client.delete_project(project) -> None   # its datasets are kept; only call when the person asks
Client.list_uploads(project=None, no_project=False, created_by=None, status=None, sort="created",
                    direction="desc", limit=20, cursor=None) -> (list[Upload], next_cursor)
Client.get_upload(upload_id) -> Upload   # .id .name .visibility ("account"|"private") .project_name .shared_with_count
Client.update_upload(upload_id, name=None, project=<unchanged>, private=None) -> Upload
    # project=None removes it from its project; private=True/False changes visibility. Only creator or account admin.
Client.list_members() -> list[Member]    # .user_id .email .display_name
Client.get_upload_shares(upload_id) -> list[Member]
Client.set_upload_shares(upload_id, users) -> list[Member]
    # REPLACES the list. users: user ids, e-mail addresses or Members. Only for private datasets.
    # Do not change visibility or share data unless the person asks.

Client.create_batch(pipeline_id: str, inputs: list[dict], *, use_latest_version=False, name=None,
                    wait_for_slot=False, slot_timeout=None) -> Batch
    # inputs: [{"slot": "input", "upload_id": upload_id}]
    # A user may have 20 batches queued or running (an account 50); one more -> 429 quota_exceeded.
    # wait_for_slot=True waits (Retry-After) and tries again instead of raising.

Client.run_many(jobs, *, max_active=4, poll_interval=10.0, dest_dir=None, use_latest=False,
                stop_on_failure=False, on_progress=None) -> list[RunResult]
    # THE way to run many batches: at most max_active (1..20) in flight, next starts when one ends.
    # job: {"pipeline": Pipeline|id, "upload_id"|"inputs"|"paths": ..., "name"?: str, "slot"?: "input"}
    # RunResult: .status ("complete"|"failed"|"cancelled"|"error"), .batch_id, .error, .paths, .job, .batch
    # on_progress(summary): {"total","done","failed","running","waiting","result"}
    # Never write a loop of create_batch() for many datasets.

Client.get_batch(batch_id: str) -> Batch

Client.list_batches(
    status: str | None = None, upload_id: str | None = None, created_by: str | None = None,
    sort: str = "created", direction: str = "desc", limit: int = 20, cursor: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[list[Batch], str | None]  # (batches, next_cursor); next_cursor is None on the last page
    # No pipeline filter server-side -- filter batches' pipeline_id yourself for one pipeline only.

Client.wait_for_batch(
    batch_id: str,
    poll_interval: float = 5.0,
    timeout: float | None = None,
    on_progress: Callable[[Batch], None] | None = None,
) -> Batch
    # Polls until status == "complete" (returns) or "failed"/"cancelled" (raises BatchFailedError,
    # code "batch_failed" / "batch_cancelled").
    # on_progress is called once per status change, e.g. on_progress=print.
    # Raises TimeoutError if timeout is set and exceeded.

Client.run(
    pipeline: str | dict,          # a Pipeline, or a bare pipeline id string
    paths: str | os.PathLike | list[str | os.PathLike],
    dest_dir: str | os.PathLike,
    *,
    slot: str = "input",
    name: str | None = None,
    poll_interval: float = 5.0,
    timeout: float | None = None,
    on_progress: Callable[[Batch], None] | None = None,
    on_upload_progress: Callable[[str, int, int], None] | None = None,  # same as upload_files(on_progress=)
    project: str | dict | None = None,   # same as upload_files(project=)
    private: bool = False,               # same as upload_files(private=)
) -> list[str]  # local file paths downloaded
    # Shortcut = upload_files() + create_batch() + wait_for_batch() + download_artifacts()
    # in one call, for the common single-input-slot case.

Client.download_artifacts(batch_id: str, dest_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> list[str]
    # Files: <output_type>_<id8>.<format>. A folder result's download_url is an API path, resolved through the
    # API (v3.5.1+); the file you get is then the folder's results.zip, still named by format.

# Typed result tables (rows are dict subclasses: Detection, Segment, LinearFeature, TreeRecord).
# table: "detections" | "segments" | "linear_features" | "tree_inventory"
Client.list_detections(batch_id, step_id=None, class_=None, confidence_min=None, bbox=None,
                       limit=1000, cursor=None) -> tuple[list[Detection], str | None]
Client.list_segments(...same filters...) -> tuple[list[Segment], str | None]          # e.g. tree crowns
Client.list_linear_features(...same filters...) -> tuple[list[LinearFeature], str | None]  # e.g. wheel ruts
Client.list_tree_inventory(batch_id, step_id=None, species=None, dbh_min=None, dbh_max=None,
                           limit=1000, cursor=None) -> tuple[list[TreeRecord], str | None]
Client.iter_results(batch_id, table, **filters) -> Iterator[row]   # all pages
Client.get_results(batch_id, table, **filters) -> list[row]
Client.results_geojson(batch_id, table, **filters) -> dict          # GeoJSON FeatureCollection, WGS84
Client.save_results(batch_id, dest_dir, tables=None) -> list[str]  # <table>.geojson per table with rows
# bbox = (min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat) or "minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat"
```

## Pipeline and Batch objects

`Pipeline` and `Batch` are real `dict` subclasses -- every key is available both ways:
```python
pipeline["id"] == pipeline.id
pipeline["name"] == pipeline.name
batch["status"] == batch.status
batch["id"] == batch.id
```
`Pipeline` fields: `id`, `name`, `description`, `graph` (internal node chain, not needed for normal
use), `account_id`, `sens_id`, `created_at`.
`Batch` fields: `id`, `status` (`"queued"` | `"running"` | `"complete"` | `"failed"` | `"cancelled"`), `steps`
(list of `{id, node_id, status, error, log_tail, ...}`), `error_message`, `created_at`,
`started_at`, `completed_at`.

## Errors

```python
forestsens.ForestSensAPIError(status: int, code: str, message: str, details: Any)
    # Raised whenever a request itself fails (auth, validation, quota, not_found, ...).
    # .status, .code, .message, .details

forestsens.BatchFailedError(batch: dict)  # subclass of ForestSensAPIError, code="batch_failed"
    # Raised specifically by wait_for_batch() when the batch reaches status "failed"
    # (the request succeeded; the batch itself failed later).
    # .batch is the full Batch -- .batch["steps"] has each failed step's error/log_tail.
```

## Known gotchas

- The slot name is `"input"` for every pipeline in the current catalog -- `run()` defaults to it.
- `upload_files()`'s folder expansion is top-level only (not recursive) and skips dotfiles.
- `Batch.status` is `"queued"` / `"running"` / `"complete"` / `"failed"` / `"cancelled"` -- never `"done"`; treat
  an unknown value as "not finished". `gateway_host` may be given with or without `https://`.
- `sens` is `"drone"` (pipelines expect `.jpg` input) or `"point"` (pipelines expect `.las`/`.laz`).
- This client covers uploads, datasets, projects and sharing, batches, artifact download and the typed result
  tables -- no API-key management (reachable directly over HTTP with the same `X-Api-Key` header against
  `/v1-key/...`).
- Result rows: `class` is a Python keyword, so use `row["class"]` or `row.class_`. `batch["results"]` says which
  tables a batch has (`{count, href}` or None). Big tables are paged (1000 rows); `get_results()` follows all pages
  and waits out a `429 rate_limited`.
- Error codes you will meet: `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403), `not_found` (404),
  `storage_limit_exceeded` (413, retrying does not help: delete or split data, or ask for a higher limit),
  `validation_error` (422; completing an upload with missing files lists them in `.details`),
  `rate_limited` / `quota_exceeded` (429, wait the `Retry-After` seconds). Do not retry in a tight loop.

## Minimal complete example

```python
from forestsens import Client

client = Client()  # FORESTSENS_GATEWAY_HOST / FORESTSENS_API_KEY env vars
pipeline = client.find_pipeline("Orthophoto (fast)")
paths = client.run(pipeline, "path/to/photos", dest_dir="downloads", on_progress=print)
```

---
Platform-side instructions for agents (HTTP details, errors, limits): the `llms.txt` served next to the API
documentation, at `https://<your host>/api-docs/llms.txt`.
For humans, worked multi-step examples, and design rationale: see [Readme.md](Readme.md) and
[docs/examples.md](docs/examples.md).
